task.description:
Produce the design artefact for ISS-0430 (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY as the BEAM<->Postgres push channel). Read docs/issues/ISS-0430.yaml in full -- it is the task, not background, and its 'SEQUENCING NOTE' paragraph carries the corrected framing (REQ-214 and ISS-0425's own REQ-219/REQ-220 have all shipped; this is a retrofit question against two already-existing pollers, not a greenfield sequencing choice). Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0430-20260905/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json's result.summary in full -- it carries, quoted from actual source, both pollers' exact poll intervals/config keys/claim-query shapes, the current supervision-tree placement (Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure / Pollers / PollersBreaker / Http), and decision 0003 Dimension B's verbatim :prefix-scoping mechanism plus the flag that LISTEN/NOTIFY has no :prefix/schema-scoping concept at all. Do not re-read those source files from scratch -- build from that evidence.

Write ONE design artefact to lib/letflow/design/ (pick a filename following this project's existing convention, e.g. iss0430-notify-listen-decision.md) that explicitly answers ALL FIVE named design questions from the issue text (connection ownership, multi-tenancy, payload limit, delivery semantics, test story) PLUS the reframed retrofit-vs-not question for the two already-shipped pollers. This is a DECISION document, not an implementation: no .ex file bodies, no migration DDL beyond a schema sketch if genuinely needed for the payload-limit answer, no @spec-heavy interface unless it is illustrative of the decision being made (e.g. sketching what a Postgrex.Notifications child_spec placement would look like is fine; writing the actual GenServer callback bodies is not).

QUESTION 2 (multi-tenancy) IS THE HARDEST PART AND MUST BE REASONED THROUGH CONCRETELY, NOT HAND-WAVED. ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis states plainly: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY channels are database-global with zero schema/:prefix concept, while Letflow's entire tenant-isolation invariant (INV-1, decision 0003 Dimension B) is a physical Postgres-SCHEMA boundary enforced per-query via Ecto's :prefix option -- there is no connection-level or session-level tenant context to lean on either (decision 0003's own 2026-08-17 addendum explicitly rejected building one). So a NOTIFY issued from within tenant A's schema context (e.g. a trigger on a tenant-schema table) is, by Postgres's own design, visible to ANY backend listening on that channel name, full stop -- there is no server-side mechanism that scopes it. Concretely reason through and choose (or reject) one of these approaches, or propose a better one, and justify the choice against INV-1's severity (BLOCKER, no MAJOR/MINOR tier for cross-tenant exposure):
  (a) a single shared channel, with the NOTIFY payload carrying only an opaque routing id (e.g. a service_task_dispatches.id or timers.id) that is NEVER tenant-identifying on its own -- the LISTENer, on receiving the id, does a normal prefix-scoped Repo.get(prefix: expected_tenant_schema) fetch, and if the row isn't found under that tenant's schema (because it belongs to another tenant), the fetch simply returns nothing and the id is discarded/ignored. This treats the NOTIFY as a pure 'something changed, go poll now' wake-up signal, never as a data-bearing or even tenant-identifying message -- work out explicitly whether this design leaks ANYTHING (row-existence-adjacent timing signal, id-space cross-tenant enumeration risk if ids are sequential and correlatable) and state the verdict;
  (b) per-tenant channel naming (e.g. NOTIFY "dispatch_ready_<tenant_schema>") with the LISTENer(s) subscribing only to channels for schemas it is entitled to see -- work out whether this actually helps given a single BEAM-side Postgrex.Notifications connection typically needs to listen application-wide (i.e. it would need to LISTEN on every tenant channel anyway, which is the same exposure as (a) unless something else changes) and whether the channel name itself becomes a tenant-enumeration surface (a channel-name list leaks which schemas/tenants exist to anyone who can query pg_listening_channels or similar);
  (c) any other mechanism you can concretely justify.
  Do not present a menu without a decision -- CHOOSE one, and state explicitly what a compromised/malicious listener process (in a hypothetical future multi-listener design) could and could not learn from the channel/payload under your chosen scheme.

QUESTION 5 (test story) -- investigate the Ecto/Postgrex ecosystem's actual precedent for testing NOTIFY under Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox (which rolls back every test transaction, so a NOTIFY issued inside a sandboxed test transaction is never committed and never fires -- Postgres only delivers NOTIFY on COMMIT). Consider Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox's shared mode (a non-transactional sandbox mode that allows real commits, typically used for testing across-process behavior) as one candidate, and consider this project's own ISS-0031 precedent if it's still applicable (referenced in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's worked examples as 'running one assertion via a checked-out non-sandboxed connection' for an analogous DDL-visibility sandbox limitation) as another. State a concrete, buildable test strategy -- not merely 'this needs more research'.

All 5 questions plus the retrofit question must each get their own clearly-headed section. State explicitly (AC2/AC3): Postgres remains the source of truth, no state travels in a NOTIFY payload (identifiers/routing hints only, always treated as untrusted on receipt), and polling is RETAINED as a reconciliation backstop -- name the specific retained poll interval(s) for both pollers under your recommendation (they are currently 5000ms/5s each per the diagnosis). State explicitly (AC5) where a Postgrex.Notifications connection (or connections -- decide how many) would sit in the CURRENT, ALREADY-SHIPPED tree (Infrastructure / Pollers / PollersBreaker / Http) -- as a new child of Infrastructure, a new sibling supervisor, or inside Pollers itself -- and justify against the existing ordering/restart-intensity reasoning in those modules' own moduledocs (do not silently contradict ISS-0429's or ISS-0451's already-settled ordering guarantees). State explicitly (AC6) whether retrofitting the two already-shipped pollers is worth doing, with reasoning, or whether the answer is 'not now' with a stated reason -- 'not worth it, keep polling' is a legitimate outcome if argued against the round-trip evidence, not chosen by default. State explicitly (AC7) that the dev-host 1.3ms figure is ~92% Docker Desktop network overhead and a co-located deployment measures ~0.11ms, and ground any recommendation in ELIMINATED ROUND TRIPS (e.g. 'N idle tenants x M sweeps/minute x 2 pollers, each currently paying a full round-trip that finds nothing') rather than the raw millisecond figure. Confirm explicitly (AC8) that no consumer implementation is included -- this is a decision document.

Once done, complete this handoff per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4, commit the design artefact and the handoff file, and route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
acceptance_criteria: A design artefact exists under lib/letflow/design/ and is committed
All five original design questions (connection ownership, multi-tenancy, payload limit, delivery semantics, test story) are answered explicitly, each under its own heading

The multi-tenancy answer names a specific concrete mechanism (not a menu of options) and states what a listener could/could not learn under it, reasoned against decision 0003 Dimension B's actual :prefix mechanism and its stated absence of any connection/session-level tenant context
The design states Postgres remains the source of truth and NOTIFY payloads carry only identifiers/routing hints, always treated as untrusted
The design states polling is retained as a reconciliation backstop, naming the specific retained interval(s) for both Letflow.Scheduler.Poller and Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller

The design places the LISTEN connection owner concretely within the CURRENT supervision tree (Infrastructure/Pollers/PollersBreaker/Http) and justifies the placement against that tree's own already-documented ordering/restart-intensity guarantees
The design states explicitly whether retrofitting the two already-shipped pollers is recommended, with reasoning either way
Any performance claim cites eliminated round trips, not the raw dev-host millisecond figure, and explicitly notes the ~92%-Docker-overhead / ~0.11ms-co-located caveat
The test story names a concrete, buildable strategy for testing NOTIFY delivery under Ecto's sandboxed test suite
No implementation code (.ex bodies, migrations beyond an illustrative schema sketch if truly needed) is present in the artefact
next_action names CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR as the next step
